inline.s: The piercing of the Governing vessel (Dumai) marks the completion of the fourth step.

The Conception vessel (Renmai) is the sea of all the yin channels, and the Governing vessel (Dumai) is the meeting of all the yang channels. When the Conception and Governing vessels flow freely, the twelve channels can progressively open unobstructed, disease has no place to lodge, and health and long life are secured. Zhuangzi says:
“Following the Governing vessel as a path, one can protect the body, can complete life, can nourish one's parents, and can live out one's years.”
(From Zhuangzi · The Nourishing of Life.)

blocks.text: Step Five: The Primordial Spirit Stores Strength and Nurtures the Vitality of Life

inline.s: The so-called primordial spirit (yuánshén) is the innate power of the brain's regulation and control, opposed to the conscious knowing-spirit (shíshén). The conscious knowing-spirit is the state of mind that is conscious and intentional. The primordial spirit and the conscious spirit stand in the relationship of substance and function: the primordial spirit is the substance and the conscious spirit is the function. When there is no thought, it is the primordial spirit; if the thought stirs but slightly, the primordial spirit is transformed into the conscious spirit. With the fourth step the Governing vessel has been pierced, and kidney qi continually irrigates the brain marrow, so that the power of the primordial spirit is continually replenished. The mind governs the spirit brightness; only when the mind's qi shines upward into the brain can it perform its full function of regulation and control.

The meaning of “the primordial spirit stores strength and nurtures the vitality of life” is that the mental state of deeply entering stillness — “tranquil and empty of things” — is precisely the primordial spirit, and it can cause the substance and motive power of life — “essence, qi, and spirit (jīng, qì, shén)” — to be stored and combined, thereby nurturing a vigorous vitality of life. This step of practice (“the primordial spirit stores strength and nurtures the vitality of life”) is carried out in a state of deep stillness.

[Entering stillness (rujing)] This refers, in the course of qigong practice, to the clear awareness that arises on the basis of a quiet mind and concentrated attention — a state of practice in which one maintains single-minded attention, relaxed and comfortable. Entering stillness is neither the ordinary state of being awake nor falling asleep. It is not the cessation of all thoughts, nor is it drowsiness and confusion; rather, it is one thought replacing ten thousand thoughts, while still maintaining the intention of the practice. For the practitioner: if during practice the intention of the practice is lost entirely, it is like a boat that has lost its rudder, so that in a state of daze one goes astray — this is something to be careful of.
Method: after the Conception-Governing cycle is formed, one generally still concentrates the attention on the lower dantian (cinnabar field),
and at this point there is no need to pay attention to the breathing

. After the Governing vessel is pierced, the various channels open one after another. If there is a moving force at the crown point (baihui) on top of the head, one may also concentrate the attention on the crown. Grasp this flexibly; this is called “when there is desire, contemplate the aperture; when there is no desire, contemplate the wonder.” As the practice advances, it will naturally strengthen the body and health, develop wisdom, and give rise to even better and more wonderful states.

[The upper dantian (shang dantian)] The upper dantian is the place where the hundred vessels meet. By constantly guarding this aperture one can develop wisdom, preserve life, and dissolve and connect with the primordial undifferentiated [qi]. When true qi is active at the upper dantian and the brain's innate power functions well, the better is the regulation and control over the whole body. [When there is desire, contemplate the aperture; when there is no desire, contemplate the wonder] This means: while practicing, if there are stray thoughts, then concentrate the attention on the lower dantian and use one thought to replace ten thousand thoughts; and after entering stillness, once the upper dantian responds, one may with a still mind guard the upper dantian and experience that mysterious state.

Time: three times a day, or more, each session one hour or longer. Generally, the longer the time the better. Only after about a month do the various stirring phenomena in the body gradually disappear, leaving only the phenomenon of the power at the lower and upper dantian becoming more concentrated and vigorous.

Effects: According to the body's manifestations, especially the magnetic force of mutual attraction between the dantian and the crown point on the head, the innate power of the cerebral cortex is strengthened and the endocrine system becomes coordinated and vigorous. This power has form and color; the deeper the practice, the more clearly and vividly it manifests, the better the regulation of the body's physiological functions, the fuller the true qi, and the more it continually compensates and strengthens the body's metabolic functions, giving full play to the body's latent power. Because vitality is vigorous, the resistance to disease and immunity is strengthened, so that common pathogenic factors can be reduced or even avoided, and even chronic intractable illnesses can be improved or cured. Persisting in the practice, one attains the effect of physical and mental health and of lengthening life.

The above five steps are the basic outline of the true method in the course of still-practice cultivation. In practice, because each person's physique differs and the concrete conditions are not the same, the effects and manifestations also vary from person to person while being broadly similar. In view of this, when practicing one must both follow the natural and apply flexibly without being artificially rigid, and also abide by certain requirements, advance patiently, and persist without ceasing, and not let oneself run freely — this is truly the essential key to success.

blocks.text: Points to Be Known in Practice

inline.s: In practicing the true method, one must establish an unwavering faith, persist without ceasing, not seek quick results, and not shrink back from difficulty. During the period of practice, follow the natural; do not cling to delusive thoughts or force the pursuit. Otherwise, haste makes waste: the more single-mindedly one pursues with impatience, the less progress one makes; the more harmonious and natural one's state of mind, the more lively the movement of true qi, and the more evident the progress. This is because willful clinging and delusive thoughts become stray thoughts that disturb the movement of true qi. “When one is tranquil and empty of things, true qi follows” is precisely this meaning.

During the course of practice, because many physiological changes occur in the body and various stirring phenomena appear, one should take them calmly, without panic and without willful pursuit; they will disappear after a short while.

. For those new to the true method, because the attention must be concentrated, a relatively quiet environment is better. However, do not overemphasize this point. While practicing, avoid interference from others. If there is unexpected interference during practice (such as a sudden sound, someone calling out urgently, or someone rushing into the practice room), do not panic; slowly relax the attention. After temporarily concluding the practice, slowly rise and deal with it, and after returning to calm resume practice. When regulating the breath, inhale and exhale through the nose, attend to the exhalation, and let the inhalation be natural; do not breathe through the mouth.

. Take care not to practice by force when very hungry, very full, very angry, or very frightened, or during other emotional excitements. When there is wind, rain, or thunder, do not sit for the time being, lest it give the mind a violent shock and cause discomfort.

. Concentrating the attention on the dantian is a principle the true method maintains throughout. When the true qi at the dantian becomes full to a certain degree, it naturally flows along the channels. The power of this movement is based on the magnitude of the dantian's power. Do not guide it with the will; let it be natural — going when it should go, stopping when it should stop. Subjective guiding will cause deviations.

. Those who use this method, before the passage has been opened, should preserve their energy and moderate sexual activity, to avoid affecting the progress of the practice. Women during their menstrual period should not concentrate on the lower dantian but may concentrate on the middle dantian (the pit of the stomach). In the early stage of pregnancy (
months) one cannot practice; in the middle and later stages one may practice.

In the process of practicing the five-step method, the active phenomena in the body are many and varied. The ancients summed them up into eight kinds, called the “eight touchings.” Sometimes one feels the body to be very “large,” sometimes very “small”; sometimes the body feels very “light,” and sometimes there is the phenomenon of the body being “heavy” as a great stone; sometimes one feels the body very “cool,” while the “hot” feeling appears fastest and most often; there are also “tickling” and “numbing” feelings. Besides the “eight touchings” above, there are even more dynamics in actual practice, such as spontaneous movement, the sensation of light, and phenomena of the residual and the anomalous.

All these phenomena are manifestations of true qi moving in different forms within the body, and all are positive and beneficial. Some people, encountering these phenomena, call in a doctor; but the doctor, not understanding, indiscriminately prescribes medicine, which is harmful. Some people, not understanding this principle, make it a mental burden. Some people, out of curiosity, pursue these phenomena, and the more they attend to them the stronger they become, until they cannot be controlled. All such cases are due to not having clearly explained the principle. Once one understands the laws of the movement of true qi, one can avoid incorrect thoughts and actions. When encountering the stirring phenomena above, one need not pursue them out of curiosity, and still less panic; just sit quietly and practice, concentrate on the dantian, and after a while they subside.

blocks.text: The Relationship of Movement and Stillness

inline.s: Movement and stillness are the two aspects of opposition and unity in the movement of things in the universe. The true method effectively uses the relationship of stillness and movement to promote the movement of true qi and enable the organism to better give play to its vitality of life, so as to achieve the aim of eliminating disease and prolonging life.

Where there is movement there must be stillness, and where there is stillness there must be movement. When stillness reaches its extreme, movement arises; when movement reaches its extreme, it returns to stillness. Stillness is the basis of movement, and movement is the expression of the power of stillness. Movement is absolute, stillness relative. In the physiological activity of the human body, this law cannot be escaped either. The body belongs to yin and governs stillness; true qi belongs to yang and governs movement. If qi leaves the body it has nothing to cling to; if the body has no qi it becomes a lump of dead matter. Only when yin and yang are mutually rooted, movement and stillness nurture each other, and body and qi coexist together, is there a lively, vibrant vitality.

What the five-step method of true-qi movement calls stillness is to make the body quiet and, with undivided attention, regulate the breath and propel the movement of true qi, so as to pierce through the Conception and Governing vessels and connect the channels. In this process the stirring phenomena in the body are many and varied, and the functions of the various parts of the body are in an active, vigorous, and vibrant state. Where is this stillness and concentration? This is nothing but a very vigorous, very natural, very orderly movement of true qi — this is called “when stillness reaches its extreme, movement arises.” The so-called stillness can only be called a temporary, relative stillness with regard to external reactions or mental activity.

The movement of a living being is absolute, and stillness relative. Those who practice still practices, though they engage in no postural activity, also pass from the active to the non-active. During practice, in cultivating true qi to connect the channels, the three fields of the front and the three gates of the back all have very intense activity. Especially when attacking the three gates of the back, the force of true qi's activity is not subject to human will, but one is controlled by a powerful surging force. This force is formed by “when stillness reaches its extreme, movement arises” and “when movement reaches its extreme, it returns to stillness.” People are familiar with and welcome “when stillness reaches its extreme, movement arises,” knowing that one must rely on this motive force to attack the gates, but of the phenomenon of “when movement reaches its extreme, it returns to stillness” they are utterly ignorant, giving rise to doubt and not knowing what to do. In fact, when things move to a certain degree, they must necessarily become still to rest and recuperate, so as to move again. This is an everyday natural phenomenon. After true qi moves for a time, it must settle and rest, and cultivate an even greater force. Therefore, if during practice one suddenly finds that the sensation at the dantian disappears, or that true qi moves and stops by fits and starts, all this is normal; do not be doubtful. Only by continuing with ease to cultivate the power at the dantian can one naturally make true qi become active again.

In short, the levels of the method of true-qi movement — refining essence into qi, refining qi into spirit, and refining spirit to return to emptiness — are all accomplished by giving play to the natural law of “when stillness reaches its extreme, movement arises; when movement reaches its extreme, it returns to stillness; stillness and movement nurture each other.”

As verified clinically, for hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, liver and gallbladder diseases, early cirrhosis, gastrointestinal diseases, diseases of the urinary and reproductive systems, chronic nephritis, rheumatoid arthritis, cervical spondylosis, neurotic symptoms, endocrine disorders, stubborn skin diseases, and so forth —

-odd kinds of functional and organic diseases it shows marked efficacy. What is even more gratifying is that it can also stimulate the body's interferon and enhance the body's immune function, and is of great benefit to the treatment of early-stage cancer patients and their postoperative recovery. Therefore, the five-step practice of the study of true-qi movement has an evident effect in curing various chronic, intractable, and stubborn diseases, and is also effective for acute diseases; moreover, it treats both the root and the branch, with no side effects whatever.
